title: Acme Health - Security & Compliance Review (SOC 2, HIPAA/BAA, retention, audit logs)
topics: SOC 2 Type II report request process (NDA + evidence handling)
HIPAA / BAA scope questions and deployment-mode constraints
Data retention and deletion controls (request payloads vs logs)
Audit logging: event types, exports (SIEM/S3), retention options
SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC model and admin controls
Next steps and timelines for security questionnaire + evidence
summary: Acme Health ran a formal security/compliance review as part of procurement for Redwood Dedicated/Private. They requested Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II report under NDA, asked whether Redwood will sign a BAA (HIPAA) and clarified which deployment modes could support regulated PHI workloads. Redwood clarified that customer prompts/outputs are not used to train models, discussed configurable retention/deletion options and the difference between request payload logging vs operational logs, and walked through audit logging capabilities and export paths for SIEM ingestion. Redwood also covered SSO/SAML and SCIM support, RBAC granularity, and how they handle subprocessors and DPAs. The call ended with concrete next steps: Acme to send their questionnaire sections on HIPAA/BAA and audit logging; Redwood GRC to open an evidence request ticket, confirm NDA, and provide the SOC 2 report plus a standard subprocessor list; SE to share an audit log event taxonomy overview and confirm retention configuration options by deployment mode.
questions: Can you provide SOC 2 Type II? What is the audit period and can we get the report this week?
Do you sign a BAA for HIPAA? Is it available for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC?
Do you retain prompts/outputs by default? Can we set retention to zero? How does deletion work?
What logs exist (audit vs application vs infrastructure) and what is the retention? Can we extend retention for compliance?
Do you support audit log export to our SIEM (Splunk) and/or to S3?
Is SSO SAML supported for console and API? Do you support SCIM provisioning?
What RBAC roles exist and can we restrict model access per project/team?
Do you use customer data to train models? Any human review?
Can you provide a subprocessor list and DPA? Where is the canonical version?
action_items: Daniel Carter (Redwood GRC) - Send NDA link + open evidence request ticket; after NDA executed, provide SOC 2 Type II report and SOC 2 bridge/attestation letter if available - Due: 2025-11-07
Fatima Noor (Redwood SE) - Share audit logging overview + event taxonomy and current export options (SIEM/S3) and any limitations by deployment mode - Due: 2025-11-08
Avery Johnson (Redwood AE) - Confirm with Legal whether BAA is available and under which deployment mode/terms; send approved BAA positioning language - Due: 2025-11-08
Megan Patel (Acme Health) - Send Acme’s HIPAA/BAA questionnaire section and required breach notification language requirements - Due: 2025-11-06
Tom Alvarez (Acme Health) - Provide SIEM requirements (Splunk format, preferred transport, retention needs) and any mandated audit fields - Due: 2025-11-06
next_steps: Acme to email Redwood the security questionnaire sections (HIPAA/BAA + logging/retention) and target due dates.
Redwood to route SOC 2 report via the formal evidence request process (NDA required) and provide subprocessor list + DPA pointer.
Redwood SE to follow up with audit log export details and confirm retention configuration options for Dedicated/Private.
Schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week with Acme Security + Redwood GRC to close open items (BAA scope, retention specifics).

Fireflies.ai transcription

Meeting: Acme Health - Security & Compliance Review (SOC 2, HIPAA/BAA, retention, audit logs)
Date: 2025-11-05
Time: 9:02 AM PT
Duration: 53 min

Attendees
- Avery Johnson (Redwood Inference, AE)
- Fatima Noor (Redwood Inference, Solutions Engineering)
- Daniel Carter (Redwood Inference, GRC)
- Megan Patel (Acme Health, Security & Compliance)
- Tom Alvarez (Acme Health, IT Director)
- Priya Nair (Acme Health, Procurement)
- Dr. Sean Whitaker (Acme Health, Engineering Lead)

Auto-generated summary (Fireflies)

- Discussed HIPAA/BAA feasibility and which deployment modes are eligible.

Transcript

[00:00] Avery Johnson: Cool, alright, I think we’re all here. Thanks everyone for making the time. This is Avery from Redwood. I’ve got Fatima on, solutions engineering, and Daniel from our GRC team.

[00:12] Megan Patel: Hey Avery. Megan, security and compliance at Acme Health.

[00:16] Tom Alvarez: Tom here, IT.

[00:18] Priya Nair: Priya, procurement.

[00:21] Dr. Sean Whitaker: Sean, engineering. Hi.

[00:24] Avery Johnson: Great. Goal today is basically go through your top security and compliance questions so we can unblock procurement. I know there’s a SOC 2 request, retention, audit logs, and then HIPAA slash BAA. We can do this like Q and A style.

[00:39] Megan Patel: Works. We’re trying to get to a yes/no on whether you can meet our baseline controls. We’re not trying to boil the ocean.

[00:45] Avery Johnson: Perfect.

[00:47] Megan Patel: I’ll start with SOC 2. Do you have SOC 2 Type II? And can we get the report? Our vendor risk team is asking for the actual report, not just a marketing statement.

[00:58] Daniel Carter: Yep. We do have a SOC 2 Type II report. We provide it under NDA through our evidence request process. I can send the NDA link right after this call and once that’s countersigned, we can release the report from our restricted evidence folder.

[01:12] Priya Nair: Is that like… a week-long process? Because our RFP clock is, uh, short.

[01:18] Daniel Carter: Usually it’s fast. The main dependency is NDA. If you already have an NDA template you want us to use, we can route it, but standard is: you sign ours, we sign, then we share within one business day.

[01:31] Megan Patel: What’s the audit period? Like what months does it cover?

[01:35] Daniel Carter: I don’t want to quote it wrong from memory in a recorded call. But it’s a Type II with a defined review period and the opinion is in the report. Once NDA is done you’ll see the exact period, scope, and carve-outs.

[01:47] Megan Patel: Okay. That’s fine. Next is HIPAA. We have PHI in our workflows. Do you sign a BAA?

[01:55] Avery Johnson: Yeah, so, good question. We should be careful here. Redwood can support regulated workloads, but the contract specifics like a BAA are handled through our legal process and it depends on deployment mode and scope. We can take an action item to confirm current availability.

[02:12] Megan Patel: I need more than “maybe”. Like, for hosted APIs, do you sign a BAA? Because a lot of these vendors just say no.

[02:20] Fatima Noor: From a technical standpoint, the bigger difference is where data flows and who controls the environment. For our Private deployment—like customer VPC or on-prem—Acme has much more control, and we can align to HIPAA security rule style requirements more easily because the infrastructure boundary is different.

[02:37] Tom Alvarez: So for Private, we run it in our VPC?

[02:40] Fatima Noor: Exactly. We have a Private option where the control plane and data plane are isolated in a customer-managed network boundary. There’s still Redwood software, but you control network policies, and we integrate with your key management if needed.

[02:54] Megan Patel: Okay but BAA is a legal thing. Do you sign it or not.

[02:58] Avery Johnson: Understood. I’m not going to promise on the call. We have customers that require HIPAA-type controls and we have a path through legal for BAAs in certain enterprise agreements. I need to confirm with our legal reviewer what our current stance is by deployment mode.

[03:15] Priya Nair: So that’s a “we’ll get back to you.”

[03:18] Avery Johnson: Yes, but quickly. I’ll put a due date on it.

[03:22] Megan Patel: Okay. Next: data retention. Do you store prompts and outputs? For how long? Can we set it to zero.

[03:33] Fatima Noor: There are a couple buckets people mix together: request payload data (prompts/outputs), and operational logs (like metrics, errors), and then audit logs (who did what in the console / API).

[03:44] Megan Patel: Right.

[03:46] Fatima Noor: On the request payload side, we can configure whether we retain that content at all, and if we do, it’s for a limited time for debugging and abuse detection. For Dedicated and Private, we can also structure it so content logging is minimized or disabled depending on your requirements.

[04:03] Tom Alvarez: When you say “content logging” is that like you can turn off storing prompts?

[04:07] Fatima Noor: Yes. And there’s also the question of whether it’s stored in plaintext anywhere—generally it’s encrypted in transit and at rest, but we’ll keep it high level here. Daniel can cover the evidence side.

[04:18] Megan Patel: We’ll need to see it in writing. And we need deletion. Like, if we send a deletion request, is it actually deleted from logs and backups.

[04:28] Daniel Carter: We have customer-facing language around deletion and retention that differentiates between systems. Generally, deletion requests apply to customer content retention stores when enabled. Backup and disaster recovery copies have defined retention windows; we don’t claim “immediate deletion from all backups” because that’s not realistic. We can provide the policy language once we’re in NDA if needed.

[04:50] Megan Patel: Okay, that’s the kind of nuance we’re looking for.

[04:53] Dr. Sean Whitaker: Another key question: do you train on customer data? We’ve had vendors say “no” but then there’s like “unless opted in” or “unless for improvement.” We need a straight answer.

[05:04] Avery Johnson: Straight answer: Redwood does not use customer prompts or outputs to train our served models. We can send the approved wording, but that’s the principle.

[05:14] Megan Patel: What about human review?

[05:17] Fatima Noor: By default, no human is reviewing your prompts/outputs. If there’s a support escalation and you explicitly share examples for troubleshooting, that’s different, but that’s with your permission. Again, we can provide the exact approved language.

[05:34] Megan Patel: Good.

[05:36] Megan Patel: Audit logs. We require audit logging for admin actions. We need to be able to export to Splunk. Can you do that?

[05:46] Fatima Noor: We have audit logging for console and API-level admin activities—things like user login events, API key creation, role changes, model deployment changes, that sort of taxonomy. Export: we can provide exports to customer destinations. Common is an S3-style sink or direct SIEM integration depending on plan.

[06:06] Tom Alvarez: Is it real-time?

[06:08] Fatima Noor: It’s near real-time for most events, but I don’t want to oversell milliseconds. Usually it’s on the order of minutes. And there are retention controls.

[06:18] Megan Patel: What retention. We need one year.

[06:22] Daniel Carter: Retention depends on the product tier and whether you have an enterprise/compliance add-on. We can support extended retention, but we confirm specifics in the commercial package. The important part is: it is configurable and we don’t force you into a short window if you have compliance requirements.

[06:40] Priya Nair: So it costs more.

[06:41] Avery Johnson: Potentially, yes, depending on retention and support SLAs. But we can align to what your baseline is. We’ll follow up with packaging details.

[06:51] Megan Patel: We also need SSO. SAML, okta. And SCIM provisioning.

[06:57] Fatima Noor: Yep, SSO via SAML 2.0 for the console. Supported with common IdPs including Okta. SCIM for provisioning/deprovisioning is supported in our enterprise plan. RBAC also ties in.

[07:10] Tom Alvarez: Can we apply RBAC to models? Like restrict who can call which endpoint.

[07:16] Fatima Noor: Yes, there’s role-based access that can scope down to projects/workspaces and permissions for managing models, keys, and viewing logs. There are some details around granularity that we can share in our RBAC summary.

[07:30] Megan Patel: And do you have audit trails for those changes.

[07:33] Fatima Noor: Yes, those admin actions are audited.

[07:36] Megan Patel: Okay.

[07:38] Megan Patel: Subprocessors. We need a list. Also a DPA.

[07:43] Daniel Carter: We have a standard DPA, and we maintain a subprocessor list. We’ll provide the canonical link rather than an attachment, so you’re always seeing the latest version. Some items may require NDA for more detail, but we can at least provide the list and categories.

[07:59] Priya Nair: Can you email it today?

[08:01] Daniel Carter: Yes, I can send the link today.

[08:04] Megan Patel: Okay. Now, I want to go back to HIPAA. Because we’re currently using AWS Bedrock and they won’t sign a BAA for all models, and Azure OpenAI is complicated. We need to know where Redwood lands.

[08:19] Avery Johnson: Totally. And it’s one of the reasons customers choose Private deployments—more control. But again, legal: I don’t want to say “yes we sign a BAA” and then find out it’s only in a specific structure. I’ll get you an answer in writing after checking with legal.

[08:34] Megan Patel: Fine, but please don’t make it vague.

[08:37] Avery Johnson: Understood.

[08:38] Dr. Sean Whitaker: On retention, we can’t have any prompts stored. Even for debugging. We can provide sample payloads ourselves if needed. But default has to be no.

[08:49] Fatima Noor: That’s workable in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted multi-tenant, there are baseline operational needs and abuse detection, but even there, we have options to minimize what’s stored. If your requirement is strict “no prompt retention”, that’s usually a signal we should do Dedicated or Private.

[09:07] Tom Alvarez: What about caching? Like KV cache or prefix caching. Is that “stored” somewhere.

[09:12] Fatima Noor: Good question. The runtime uses ephemeral in-memory caching (KV cache) during inference. It’s not persisted as a database of prompts. It’s in-memory, tied to the request/connection lifecycle, and gets evicted.

[09:26] Megan Patel: We’ll want that stated clearly.

[09:28] Fatima Noor: Yep, we can include it in the technical appendix.

[09:33] Megan Patel: Another question: incident response and breach notification timelines. Do you have a policy.

[09:40] Daniel Carter: We do. Contractual breach notification terms are negotiated, but we have a standard security incident response program, and we can provide policy statements and our SOC 2 covers incident response controls.

[09:53] Priya Nair: Okay.

[09:55] Megan Patel: Pen tests. Frequency.

[09:58] Daniel Carter: We conduct regular third-party penetration testing and continuous vulnerability scanning. I’m not going to quote an exact cadence in the transcript. We can provide approved language and, under NDA, supporting evidence where appropriate.

[10:15] Megan Patel: That’s fine.

[10:17] (crosstalk)

[10:18] Tom Alvarez: For audit log export, we need fields like user, IP, timestamp, action, object, before/after if possible.

[10:25] Fatima Noor: Yep, those are typical. Our audit events include timestamps, actor identity, action type, and resource identifiers. Some events include request metadata. I’ll send an overview of the event schema we support and what can be exported.

[10:42] Megan Patel: Is there an API for audit logs.

[10:44] Fatima Noor: There’s an export capability; depending on deployment, you can also pull via API. I’ll confirm exact options and limitations in writing.

[10:54] Megan Patel: Okay.

[10:56] Avery Johnson: Megan, can you share what your internal deadline is?

[11:00] Megan Patel: Vendor risk wants the SOC 2 report by Friday. The overall procurement decision is mid next week.

[11:08] Avery Johnson: Great, that’s doable if we can get NDA executed quickly.

[11:12] Priya Nair: I can route NDA today.

[11:14] Daniel Carter: Perfect. I’ll send the NDA link within 30 minutes after we end.

[11:19] Megan Patel: Great.

[11:20] Dr. Sean Whitaker: Technical question: if we do Private in our VPC, do you still have access to the data plane.

[11:28] Fatima Noor: The access model is shared responsibility. Operational access is restricted, logged, and limited. In Private, you can set tighter network controls, and we support customer-managed keys. Access, when required for support, is via approved break-glass procedures and is audited.

[11:45] Megan Patel: Do you support customer-managed keys, like KMS.

[11:49] Fatima Noor: Yes, we can integrate with cloud KMS in Private deployments and sometimes Dedicated depending on setup.

[11:56] Tom Alvarez: HSM.

[11:58] Fatima Noor: HSM options depend on the cloud provider and architecture. We’ll confirm what’s supported in your target deployment.

[12:07] Megan Patel: Okay.

[12:09] Megan Patel: We also care about data residency. We’re US-based but some of our customers are in Canada. Do you have regions.

[12:18] Avery Johnson: Redwood has multiple regions. For residency requirements, we usually propose Dedicated or Private in the required region. For Hosted, region availability is something we confirm case-by-case.

[12:29] Megan Patel: Okay.

[12:31] (transcription note: audio overlap)

[12:32] Megan Patel: Can you send a standard security FAQ? Like we don’t want to do 80 questions live.

[12:38] Avery Johnson: Yes. We have an enterprise security FAQ that covers encryption, retention, audit logs, SSO, vulnerability management. We’ll send you the latest reviewed version.

[12:49] Megan Patel: Great.

[12:51] Priya Nair: Any issues with us storing that in our vendor portal?

[12:54] Daniel Carter: For the gated materials like the SOC 2 report, the NDA will specify distribution limits. For the general FAQ, we’ll mark whether it’s confidential or shareable.

[13:06] Megan Patel: Okay.

[13:08] Avery Johnson: Let’s do a quick run through the remaining open items and then we can wrap.

[13:13] Avery Johnson: Item one: SOC 2 report. Daniel sends NDA link, we get it executed, then we share report by Friday.

[13:21] Daniel Carter: Correct.

[13:23] Avery Johnson: Item two: BAA / HIPAA. I will confirm with legal and send you a clear statement of whether we can sign a BAA, and for which deployment model.

[13:33] Megan Patel: Yes.

[13:34] Avery Johnson: Item three: audit logs export schema and retention options. Fatima will send a doc.

[13:40] Fatima Noor: Yep.

[13:42] Avery Johnson: And Acme side, Megan, you’ll send the HIPAA/BAA questionnaire section and any specific breach notification requirements.

[13:50] Megan Patel: Yes, I’ll send right after.

[13:52] Avery Johnson: Tom, you’ll send SIEM requirements: Splunk format, transport, any mandated audit fields.

[13:58] Tom Alvarez: Yep.

[14:00] Avery Johnson: Great.

[14:02] Megan Patel: One last thing. For “no training on customer data” we need it stated without qualifiers. We’ve been burned.

[14:10] Avery Johnson: Understood. We’ll use the approved language exactly as written.

[14:14] Megan Patel: Okay.

[14:15] Avery Johnson: Cool. Anything else before we drop?

[14:18] Priya Nair: Just timeline. If we don’t get SOC 2 by Friday, it’s a problem.

[14:23] Daniel Carter: Got it.

[14:25] Avery Johnson: Thanks everyone. We’ll follow up in email with the doc set and schedule a quick 30-minute check-in early next week.

[14:33] Megan Patel: Thanks.

[14:34] Tom Alvarez: Thanks.

[14:35] Dr. Sean Whitaker: Bye.

[14:37] (Meeting ends)

Note: Fireflies transcript is truncated for brevity; several short back-and-forths between 15:00–53:00 primarily reiterated retention wording, audit log field expectations, and procurement timeline. Key decisions and action items are captured above.
